title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page belongs to the 'variations on the loop equation' manuscript, which continues the Longue Marche. Grothendieck works with an abstract profinite group G^+ that is modelled on the profinite completion of GL(2,Z) or SL(2,Z), together with a distinguished normal subgroup G^natural. In the 'universal case', G^natural is Π_0, a subgroup of the profinite fundamental group Π of a modular curve (essentially P^1 minus three points, or M_{1,1}). Attached to a pair (ρ, σ) he has constructed:
- a group G_{ρ,σ}, an extension 1 → G^natural → G^natural_{ρ,σ} → γ_{ρ,σ} → 1;
- characters of γ_{ρ,σ}: ε_{3γ}, ε_{2γ} to μ and χ_γ to Ẑ^*;
- a subgroup Z_{ρ,σ} containing L_0^natural = SZ_{ρ,σ}. L_0 is the inertia (cusp) subgroup at 0, topologically generated by g_0 (relations (62)-(64) on the previous page).
Earlier, on pages 615 ff., he had worked in the concrete situation with subgroups M(1/2), M'(-j), M'''(-j) and N_ρ^! of a group M. Here M is presumably the group of automorphisms or normalizers attached to Π. M(0) is the stabilizer of the cusp 0, M^! = M(0).Π, and M_0^! = M(0).Π_0.

The problem on this page. He wants abstract analogues of those subgroups inside G_{ρ,σ}. For this he needs a subgroup of G^natural_{ρ,σ} playing the role of M_0^!. Ideally this would be G^natural_{ρ,σ} itself.

Test in the universal case (G^+ = GL(2,Z)^, G^natural = Π_0):
- One finds G_{ρ,σ} ≅ M.
- Z_{ρ,σ} = M[0]^! = M(0).L_0^Π, and L_0^natural = L_0^Π.
- G^natural_{ρ,σ} is the subgroup of M generated by Π_0 and Z_{ρ,σ}. Since L_0 together with Π_0 generates Π, this is M(0).Π = M^!, not M(0).Π_0 = M_0^!.

So the abstract definition overshoots. His diagnosis is that Z_{ρ,σ} is too big. The fix is to choose inside Z_{ρ,σ} a subgroup Z_{ρ,σ}(0), corresponding to M(0) (65), giving:
- (66) a semidirect decomposition Z_{ρ,σ} ≅ Z_{ρ,σ}(0).L_0^natural;
- (67) G_{ρ,σ} ≅ Z_{ρ,σ}(0).G^+, also semidirect.
He crossed out the companion formula for the natural-part.

The next page then defines (G^natural_{ρ,σ})_0 := Z_{ρ,σ}(0).G^natural. It also produces a standard splitting from a (ρ,σ)-equivariant map G^+ → PSL(2,Ẑ), via the Borel-type group B'_0 of matrices (μ λ; 0 1). The purpose is to recover, for abstract 'GL_2-like' profinite groups, the cusp-stabilizer and level structure needed for the loop-equation analysis.
errors: No real mathematical error. The equality 'M(0).L_0^Π = M(0).Π' on this page means the subgroup generated by Z_{ρ,σ} and Π_0. It is correct only if L_0 is not contained in Π_0, which is implicitly assumed.

The splitting Z_{ρ,σ}(0) is asserted to exist 'without difficulty' but is not constructed here. A construction is attempted on the next page via a homomorphism to PSL(2,Ẑ), which is a non-canonical choice.
On the next page, formula (68) for Z^natural_{ρ,σ} is written confusingly ('Z^natural = Z = G^natural ∩ Z'); the first equality is presumably a slip.

ideas.what: Recovering the analogue of the cusp-stabilizer subgroup M(0).Π_0 inside an abstract extension G_{ρ,σ} by splitting off the inertia group L_0 semidirectly.
ideas.modern_name: Semidirect splitting of the decomposition/inertia subgroup at a cusp (Borel-type decomposition) in profinite modular groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard group theory; the context is close to Grothendieck–Teichmüller and anabelian work on π_1 of M_{1,1} (Ihara, Nakamura, etc.)
ideas.where_published: Longue Marche (1981) treats related groups, but not this specific construction

ideas.what: A test of an abstract definition against the 'universal case' G^+ = GL(2,Z)^, G^natural = Π_0, showing that the naive definition gives M^! instead of M_0^!.
ideas.modern_name: sanity check of a definition on the universal/free case

deep.surprise_reason: This is a technical bookkeeping page inside a long unpublished construction. It corrects an overly large subgroup by choosing a semidirect complement. It contains no standalone result or connection likely to be absent from the literature beyond the general unpublished status of the manuscript.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: 'qu'il ait un groupe' should read 'qu'il y ait un sous-groupe'.
In (67), the left-hand side is likely G_{ρ,σ}, overwriting M_{ρ,σ}. This is consistent with the next page's 'G_{ρ,σ} = Z_{ρ,σ}(0).G^+'.
Struck-out heading: 'Exemple du cas universel G^ = GL(2,Z)^, avec G^natural = Π_0'. The words 'du cas' are inserted above the line.
'Il n'y a pas de difficulté [?] d'en jouer [?] définir' is more plausibly 'Il n'y a pas de difficulté, il me semble, pour définir' (uncertain).
'(on trouve G_{ρ,σ} ≃ M,' — the parenthesis opens before 'on trouve'. 'L_0^natural = L_0^Π' is an insertion above the line.
